newsitem.title: UK: Power lifts Energy Group Q1 profits.
newsitem.headline: Power lifts Energy Group Q1 profits.

text.p: Energy Group, which was spun off from Hanson Plc on Monday, said its operating profits rose 38 percent to 138 million pounds ($223.7 million) in the three months to December 31 as its power operation results improved.
Former parent Hanson Plc said total pre-tax profit, including Energy Group, fell to 157 million pounds for the same period from 248 million following a year of demergers.
The once mighty conglomerate Hanson has already hived off Imperial Tobacco and Millennium Chemicals.
After today's demerger of the Energy Group, Hanson only incorprates building material and aggregates operations.
Shares in Energy Group, which consists of U.S.-Australian Peabody Coal and Britain's regional electricity company Eastern, firmed at their debut on the London Stock Exchange.

They traded at 546-1/2 pence in mid-morning trade, which was 21-1/2 pence higher than they were trading on the grey market prior to the demerger. Hanson's shares firmed 2-1/2 pence to 290. ($1=.6168 Pound)
